methodological_rigor.justification: Cell line and organoid-based study with PROTAC-mediated protein degradation and CRISPR genetic approaches. Appropriate controls comparing AR-dependent vs. AR-negative prostate cancer models. Mechanistic validation through transcriptional analysis and pathway characterization. Limitations: limited in vivo tumor models (organoids rather than full xenografts), statistical testing not comprehensively reported for all analyses, no explicit power calculations stated, organoid response metrics somewhat subjective.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical translational research addressing AR-negative castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC-WNT), representing 11% of ~400,000 annual CRPC cases. Identifies SWI/SNF-SMARCA4 as targetable axis in this treatment-resistant subtype. Demonstrates mechanistic dependence on TCF7L2-mediated MAPK signaling. PROTAC degraders represent novel druggable modality. High clinical relevance to unmet therapeutic need in lineage-plastic CRPC.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods adequately describe cell line handling, PROTAC reagents, organoid culture conditions, and transcriptomic approaches. However, incomplete details on organoid viability assays, specific flow cytometry markers, and statistical test specifications. No explicit data availability statement. RNA-seq data likely in GEO but accession not mentioned in abstract/introduction.

novelty_literature.justification: Extends PROTAC-based SWI/SNF targeting from AR-dependent to AR-negative CRPC context, demonstrating broader applicability. Identifies TCF7L2-MAPK axis as critical in WNT-dependent CRPC, which is somewhat novel. However, SWI/SNF dependence in WNT-signaling tumors previously documented in other contexts. Contribution is meaningful but incremental application of existing concepts.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear introduction establishing clinical problem (AR-negative CRPC lineage plasticity). Methods section adequate but some details sparse (organoid assays). Results logically presented from PROTAC effects through mechanistic validation. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within lineage plasticity literature. Figures support main conclusions but could be more visually polished.

key_strengths: Identifies SWI/SNF-SMARCA4 as critical target in AR-negative CRPC-WNT subtype (11% of CRPC cases), addressing unmet therapeutic need
Mechanistic clarity: SMARCA4 depletion disrupts TCF7L2, blocking MAPK-mediated proliferation in WNT-signaling-dependent tumors
PROTAC-based approach offers reversible protein degradation modality with potential favorable toxicology vs. kinase inhibitors
Organoid models provide more physiologically relevant context than cell lines alone
key_concerns: Limited in vivo validation; organoid models show promise but full xenograft studies would strengthen claims of therapeutic efficacy
PROTAC compounds used are investigational; clinical development timeline and intellectual property landscape not discussed
Limited exploration of mechanism beyond TCF7L2; other SWI/SNF complex members and their specific roles not comprehensively characterized
Small sample sizes for organoid studies; statistical power and reproducibility across independent patient samples not established
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: competent preclinical study identifying actionable target in lineage-plastic prostate cancer. Mechanistic insights solid but limited in vivo validation and some methodological details incomplete. Appropriate for specialized oncology journals; requires further development for clinical translation.
